cases.name: the posting rules over the API: the read contracts, the refusals the API states, and one escrow per task
cases.vector: a noded with no fleet: GET /api/v0/treasury[/journal] and their read-only-ness (405/404); a nonsense budget refused 400 with the ledger unchanged; each create its own task and its own escrow (the same create twice is two tasks, never one id reused); the claim/state-machine refusals; and the rule set itself recorded as covered by the crate's own tests (the API has no write-entry endpoint)

invariants.name: the treasury starts as the mint alone: one account, no entries, a zero sum
v0 states its own spend honestly (nothing is metered)
invariants.detail: spent=0 note='v0 meters no real spend; a done task refunds its whole escrow'

invariants.name: the journal starts empty and untruncated
the treasury endpoints accept GET only (a write method is a 405 on both)
a path under the treasury that is not the journal is a 404
a budget past i64::MAX is refused 400 in the ledger's own words
a create outside the contract is refused 400 (an empty goal, a non-integer budget)
a refused create leaves the ledger and the journal exactly as they were (no id consumed)
each create is its own task: the id is handed out in order and never reused
each create opens its own escrow, minted by its own entry (no shared or double-posted escrow)
each mint names its own task (the journal has one mint per create, in create order)
a claim from an agent this node has no live session for is a 409
finishing an open task is a 409 (the ledger's state machine)
invariants.detail: {"error":"a task may not go from open to done"}

notes: the posting rules themselves are NOT exercised through the API, and this case does not invent an entry it cannot post: the daemon serves NO write-entry endpoint (the treasury surfaces are GET-only, asserted above), so a posting that breaks a rule of the schema's table is unreachable from here. The rule set is transcribed verbatim in crates/noded/src/treasury.rs (POSTING_RULES, the schema's treasury.posting_rules) and covered there by its own tests (the rule matrix, check_entry's order, the balance/overdraw/margin checks, and the mutant-killing suite), plus crates/noded/tests/treasury.rs for the API-reachable half (the mint/refund wiring, the views, the SSE frames). That is where the rest is covered; this case asserts only what this API can reach.

cases.vector: a 2-role fleet (builder + librarian) on the suite's own vsockd --admin-port --roles and noded --agents --hub-admin: uptime driven through noded and through the hub directly; write_file granted on the builder and 403 (role librarian does not grant write_file) on the librarian, with the guest's transcript proving the call never reached it; POST /stop ends the session (the transcript shows stop -> bye -> staying up), the registry drains, the VM stays running; and the artifact read-through returns the builder's file byte-exact, with an escaping path the agent's own 422

the hub's /tell: a served CID with no live session is a 409
